During the burial of their graves [as interpreted], Mario was killed with shovels, axes, and other things that these people who were there had in their hands. So what is important is that the brigade policeman who was there and who were supposed to guard us simply could not offer us any protection. And Mario Zrno was beaten by everybody, by the women who arrived there, by grandmothers, by the elderly who were grieving the deaths of their close family," would this be the correct description of what had happened in the Crnice cemetery? And this description was provided by Dragan Keskic.

utterances.speaker: VINKO ZRNO
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be provided with a document that the Defence received on the 18th February 2004. We have an ample number of copies according to Rule 68. We have an ample number of copies for the Judges, for the registry, for the Prosecutors, and our colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If Zeljko Milos in his statement to the Prosecution on the 16th February 2004 at 10.00 said as follows: "While Mr. Milos was digging graves in Crnice at the beginning of August 1993 as a prisoner of the BiH army, one of the two brothers, the Velagic brothers, Safet and Muhko, one of the two brothers hit Marko Zrno twice with a shovel. As a result of that, Mr. Zrno fainted, said Milos, and Mr. Zrno did not come back with Mr. Milos and the other detainees to the furniture salon where he had been put previously. The brothers that Zeljko Milos named are the Velagici brothers, both Bosniak Muslims. They were both civilians, said Milos, and in the cemetery they attended the burial of the dead bodies." Would this statement given by Zeljko Milos represent a correct description of the incident?

utterances.speaker: VINKO ZRNO
utterances.text: Mr. Muhko Velagic wore the uniform of the BiH army. I guarantee you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objections, because this is under Rule 68, and we certainly won't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number for these two documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will get the exhibit number DH341, and the B/C/S translation gets the exhibit number DH341/BCS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now give the floor to the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Kubura's Defence has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there anything -- is there something I could ask you? Could I ask Defence counsel something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, Defence counsel is supposed to ask the questions, but you could put the question to me and then we will see. Tell me what you wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I would like to ask Defence counsel where the other people from the list that Ms. Residovic read out are, where their -- I would like to ask them where their statements are. Can they tell us where Niko Dzaja is or Zoran Galic is? Read the names out, Ms. Residovic. Read them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has taken note of what you have said. Ms. Benjamin, do you have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Just two, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Zrno, in reply to Justice Swart's question with respect -- or the President's question with respect to being informed under the Geneva Conventions, you said you were questioned by the superiors in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. Would you be able to assist the Tribunal? Who were these superiors that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: VINKO ZRNO
utterances.text: I only know the gentleman is a lawyer who worked in Bugojno. He was from Tomislavgrad. He was a compatriot of mine, and he behaved in a very correct and fair manner. The statement I gave was signed. I answered the questions, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And as to the names that my friend read out, could you tell us with respect to the two -- aside from the two that were mentioned, could you tell us what you know of these persons now.

utterances.speaker: VINKO ZRNO
utterances.text: I know that I saw them. Niko Dzaja, I saw him for the last time at that cemetery, whereas I saw Zoran Galic later on at the stadium. And the other 18 were taken away to the BH Bank for interrogation. I never heard anything about them. As for Mr. Strujic who helped the BH army a lot, I never saw him again. So maybe they could answer those questions. Perhaps they could say where these people are now. To this very day, no one knows where they are; no one knows where their bones remain.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's the end of the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this concludes your examination. We would like to thank you for having come to testify as a witness for the Prosecution in The Hague. You have answered all the questions put to you by the Prosecution and by Defence counsel. You have also answered the questions put to you by the Judges. We have listened to your testimony very carefully, and we wish you all the best in the life you are trying to build for yourself at the moment. I would also like to wish you a good trip home. And I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom, and the Victims and Witnesses Unit will help you to go either back to the hotel or to the airport. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. But there is another question I would like to put to you, if I may. I would like to put it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead. What would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came here as a witness. I don't know the accused. Were the people accused for Bugojno Dzevad Mlaco, Abdula Jelac and Senad Dautovic? They were the main people in charge of the conflict in Bugojno. They were in charge of the entire action. This is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber is not dealing with their case, so I can't answer the question you have put to us. But I would like to thank you and I will ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give the floor to the Prosecution now. As far as the documents that I mentioned are concerned, were you able to take stock of the situation during the break? And I'll first deal with the issue of the documents and then I will give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it had to do with the previous evidence, and I thought it would be best if I said something for the sake of the transcript. I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that a document that we handed over as a document exhibit was one that we received from the Prosecution, which withdrew a witness who was supposed to be heard on a given day and before the Trial Chamber. As I hadn't explained that, when I was tendering the document into evidence, I thought that it was my duty to inform the Trial Chamber of the fact. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for that information. Ms. Benjamin, to address the issue of the documents again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, maybe I should start with the less complex ones first. And I'm happy to inform the Trial Chamber that I have some translations to hand over, and they would be the French translations to 12 documents. The Prosecution Exhibit numbers were P208, the English, P214, P223, P225, 226, 227, 264, 273, 311, 378, 379, and 380. I'm happy to hand over the French translations and ask that same be tendered into evidence, please. The English and the B/C/S have already been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. These documents have numbers in B/C/S and in English. It's necessary to give them a number in French. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The French translation of P208 gets the exhibit number P208/F; the French translation of P214 gets the exhibit number P214/F; the French translation of the exhibit P223 gets the exhibit number P223/F; the French translation of exhibit P225 gets the exhibit number P225/F; the French translation of the exhibit number P226 gets the exhibit number P226/F; the French translation of the exhibit number P227 gets the exhibit number P227/F; the French translation of the exhibit number P264 get it is exhibit number P264/F; the French translation of the exhibit number P-- I apologise, 273 get it is exhibit number P273/F; the French translation for the exhibit P311 gets the exhibit number P311/F; the French translation of the exhibit P378 gets the exhibit number P378/F; the French translation of the exhibit P379 gets the exhibit number P379/F; and the French translation of the exhibit P380 gets the exhibit number P380/F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Benjamin, you still have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With respect to the balance of translations, most of the translations have been filed in draft form and I have been informed that we will have the final drafts on all those ready on Thursday, along with the few that had no drafts at all, those will be ready for Thursday, which will have completed our translations. Then with respect to the documents that had the internal OTP numbers and we couldn't find any category as to P or to contested documents, a few more has been drawn to our attention, and with the exception of one, I would wish to make the application or to ask the Court to withdraw same, and those would be internal numbers 950, 952, 958, 959, 960, 962, 963, 964, and 965. Most of those documents are dated before the indictment period, and for reasons the Prosecution has decided to withdraw same. With respect to 953, that is the same as contested document 451. 451 apparently was tendered as an excerpt and subsequently the Court requested that the whole document be filed, and I'm told that the whole document has since been filed, so 953 is really contested document 451. I would continue in my personal capacity to ensure that we get all the documents ready and forwarded to the Trial Chamber by Thursday, as promised. I think that would have taken care of everything, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Reading the transcript, and having followed what you said, the Trial Chamber understands that the situation is as follows: You are withdrawing the documents under 959, 952, 958, 960, 962, 963, 964, and 965. You are withdrawing these documents because they are outside of the Prosecution's indictment period, so you want to withdraw them. You said that 953 is a document which is in fact identical to document 451. It appears that this is a document which is an extract, whereas 953 is the complete document. So 953 corresponds to 451. That's what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution stated that the problem of the documents has been completely resolved, apart from the fact that there are a number of documents -- a few documents that are still being translated and we will be provided with them by Thursday at the latest. Naturally, we will check this. This is what we have been doing for weeks now. But we're heading in the right direction, apparently. As I said yesterday, we will be rendering our final decision on the documents on Friday. Our decision will be rendered on Friday, as I said. It's a very long decision, as it consists of a number of pages. We are in the process of completing it. You will have it by Friday. It will be filed with the Registry at about noon or 1.00 p.m., so you should then have this document -- this written document on the admission of evidence. As you said yesterday, the -- as we said yesterday, the last hearing should be held on Friday, that should be the 23rd, the 23rd of July. According to the schedule, the hearing should start at 9.00. As I said yesterday, there will be two stages of the hearing: The registry will give us the final exhibit numbers for documents admitted in accordance with our decision which will have been rendered one week in advance. The registry will provide us with the numbers. In order to save time, the registrar could perhaps already establish -- or draft a document with the numbers in question. After that stage, the Chamber will give the floor to Ms. Benjamin so that she can officially state that the Prosecution has completed the presentation of its case. So these are the issues we will be dealing with on Friday, the 23rd of July. Which then we will be entering the framework already mentioned. We'll be following the schedule that has been referred to in an oral decision rendered yesterday. Are there any submissions that Defence counsel would like to make? Yes, Mrs. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when examining the Witness ZP, we requested that two documents be marked for identification until the documents had been translated. The documents concern DH217 ID and DH218 ID. We received the translations of these documents from CLSS today, so I would like these translations to be provided to the Chamber, to the registry, and to the Prosecution. And could final exhibit numbers be given to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin, we have two documents, DH217 and DH218. They've been marked for identification. We have now been provided with the translations of these documents. What is the Prosecution's position with regard to these two documents? DH217 is a table [as interpreted], and DH217 is the translation of a document from Mr. Bisic. These are "Instructions on Cooperation between the Civilian Protection and the Armed Forces in a Time of War in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." What is your position?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objections.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: DH218 is a table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have these two final exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document DH217 ID gets the final exhibit number DH217, and the English translation gets the exhibit number DH217/E; the document DH218 ID gets the final exhibit number DH218, and the English translation gets the exhibit number DH218/E.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have one other request to make: When examining the witness, the Judge Vlado Adamovic, the Defence counsel tendered into evidence records of an on-site investigation which had to do with the murder of four HVO members and the kidnapping of Zivko Totic. A partial translation was also provided. The Chamber admitted this into evidence, and the number was DH340. The Defence has obtained a translation of the entire record of the on-site investigation, so we suggest that the exhibit be replaced by the exhibit that has a complete translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Do you have the document with you? So DH340 only consisted of partial translations, or it was only a partial translation. We now have a complete document. Ms. Benjamin should be shown the document. The date is the 15th of April, 1993, the date of this complete document. It concerns the investigation site, and the investigation was carried out by the Judge Mirsad Strika [phoen]. Ms. Benjamin, you have no objections to raise to having the former document replaced by this new one?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, the document we have just been provided with by the Defence is under number DH340, and the former document, the old document, will be replaced by this new one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document -- the initially tendered version of DH340/E is replaced by the new tendered version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes. You still have the floor, Defence Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no other issues to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Bourgon, you have familiarised yourself with the memo. We still don't have it. We haven't had the time to have a look at it. But you have no comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would prefer to wait for the Trial Chamber to examine it, and then I'll have time to analyse the response, and perhaps at the last hearing, if necessary, I might make some submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I'll now turn to the other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no submissions to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Having dealt with all the items on the agenda, I will now -- we will now adjourn, and I will see everyone at the hearing on Friday, the 23rd of July at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of July, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.06 p.m.,
